To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that the C T transition at nucleotide 3256 of human mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is pathogenetically relevant and causes a multisystem disorder, characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction, lactic acidosis, and neurodegeneration.

the C T transition at nucleotide position 3256 of mitochondrial DNA is pathogenic for the human mitochondrial myopathy, and that it is associated with a decrease in mitochondrial protein synthesis, respiratory chain activity, and tRNA steady-state levels.
we identified a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) polymorphism (a CT transition at position 3265) in a patient and that the mutant mtDNA is associated with a multisystem disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a human disease due to a mitochondrial DNA polymorphic mutation.

the characterization of the functional and molecular abnormalities associated with a mitochondrial tRNA gene polymorphism, in order to provide a better understanding of the molecular basis of mitochondrial disorders and the mechanisms involved in the pathogenicity of mitochondrial DNA mutations.
the study of a mitochondrial DNA mutation in a human disease and its effect on the mitochondrial function at the molecular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a C T transition at mtDNA position 3256 is a pathogenetic mutation that impairs mitochondrial protein synthesis and respiratory chain activity, and that these functional defects are associated with a decreased steady-state levels of tRNA.
this mtDNA polymorphic transition is pathogenic when it is present in a high enough proportion of the mtDNA pool.
the mtDNA 3265 mutation, when present at high levels in the cell, is associated with a multisystemic disease, characterized by mitochondrial respiratory chain dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mtDNA 3265 mutation is pathogenic, that its effect depends on its proportion in the cell, and that the molecular abnormalities are related to mitochondrial protein synthesis.
the mtDNA 3,256 polymorphism is a pathogenetic mtDNA mutation that affects mitochondrial protein synthesis, leading to a multisystem mitochondrial disorder.
a single mtDNA polymorphism can have a profound effect on mitochondrial function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of mitochondrial disorders is complicated by the fact that most patients harbor heteroplasmic mtDNA mutations.

the use of transmitochondrial cybrid cell lines, harboring different proportions and ratios of mutated and normal mtDNA, can be a useful approach to investigate the pathogenic mechanism of heteroplasmic mtDNA mutations.
the use of cybrid clones harboring different proportions or only mutated mtDNA allows us to study the functional and molecular consequences of a mitochondrial mutation in a cell culture system.
